## The vapour column repair {#sec-ch08-fixvapor}

### Summary

When the borrow of @sec-ch08-borrow cannot cover a deficit from the parent vapour in the same cell, the
vapour itself goes negative and a local repair has no mass to work with. The column repair is the
fallback: it looks along the whole $x_1$ column for mass to move.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- A repair along a whole $x_1$ column, not a floor: it moves mass within the column.
- Switch: part of the conserved limiter, where a vapour row has gone negative.
- Conserves mass by weighting with cell volumes, so it repairs mass and not density.
- Gathers the column across ranks when the $x_1$ axis is split.
- Clouds tolerate an unrepairable column and clamp; vapour must throw instead.
:::

### Derivation

The scheme is a redistribution, so the thing to establish is what it conserves. It weights by cell
volume at `cell_volume` ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}), which is the point recorded in the code comment
there: a column repair that moved *densities* would not conserve mass on a non-uniform grid, because
equal densities in unequal cells are unequal masses. Weighting by volume makes the redistribution
conservative in mass.

This chapter does not port the repair, and the reason is worth stating rather than hiding: the search
itself is a device kernel reached through a dispatch call, so a numpy port would be a reimplementation
rather than a port, and a check built on it would test my reimplementation and not the code. The
conservation property above is read from the code and its comment; it is not measured here.

### Numerical method

The repair is the lambda at `split` ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}). When the $x_1$ axis is split
across ranks it gathers the column first, so the repair sees the whole column rather than one block's
piece of it.

The two callers are deliberately different, and the comment at
`repair_column` ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}) says why: clouds tolerate a column that cannot be repaired and
fall back to a clamp at `clamp_min_` ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}), while vapour must throw rather than copy
a bad gathered column back, which is the check at `err` ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}). A failure
in the vapour path is therefore a hard stop, not a silent repair.

### Tests

`test_fix_vapor_reports_failure_python` checks that an unrepairable column raises
`Failed to fix vapor`; its CUDA arm is `test_fix_vapor_reports_failure_cuda_python`.
`test_fix_vapor_counts_every_column_python` places a broken column at 32 positions with
multiple CPU threads and requires every failure to be reported
({{< code tests/test_fix_vapor_reports_failure.py main >}},
{{< code tests/test_fix_vapor_counts_every_column.py main >}};
registrations: {{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}).
These tests cover failure reporting, not successful repair's volume-weighted conservation.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- The vapour path throws when the column cannot be repaired. That is a crash, not a degraded run, and
  it is the intended behaviour rather than a defect.
- The repair needs the whole column. On a split $x_1$ axis it gathers across ranks, so it is a
  collective operation inside what is otherwise a local limiter.
:::

1. **Not ported, not measured.** The conservation claim is read from the code and its comment. No check
   in this chapter and no ctest in the repository demonstrates it.
2. **Cost.** Gathering a column is communication in the middle of the equation-of-state call. Nothing in
   the repository measures how often it fires or what it costs.
